data.name: Awliyaat
data.gender_notes: Awliyaat is used as a مذكر name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A group of people who are considered to be close to Allah, and have a special spiritual connection with Him. They are often referred to as intercessors and can provide protection and guidance to those who seek their help. The name Awliyaat carries the meaning “Friends of Allah” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Pashto. Parents who choose Awliyaat usually hope their child will grow to embody friends of allah and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a child who is believed to have a strong spiritual connection with Allah and the ability to intercede on behalf of others.
data.etymology: Awliyaat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Friends of Allah.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Awliyaat total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: أولياء
in_arabic.long_meaning: أولياء الله تعالى هم النساء الصالحات والمؤمنات اللاتي يحببنهن الله ورسوله، ذكرت في القرآن الكريم في سورة النساء و سورة التحريم، لهن مكانة عالية في الإسلام

in_urdu.name: اولیاء
in_urdu.long_meaning: اولیاء اللہ وہ نیک عورتوں اور مؤمن خواتین ہیں جنہیں اللہ تعالیٰ اور اس کے رسول محبوب رکھتے ہیں، قرآن پاک میں سورہ النساء اور سورہ التحریم میں ذکر ہے، ان کی اسلام میں بہت اہمیت ہے

in_hindi.name: अवलियात
in_hindi.long_meaning: अवलियात उन नेक औरतों और मोमिन महिलाओं को कहते हैं जिन्हें अल्लाह तआला और उसके रसूल प्यार करते हैं, कुरआन में सूरह अन्निसा और सूरह अत्तहरीम में उल्लेख है, इन्हें इस्लाम में बहुत महत्व दिया गया है

in_pashto.name: اولیا
in_pashto.meaning: ښہ غزده ښځو او مؤمنه ښځو

in_english.name: Awliyaat
in_english.long_meaning: Awliyaat refers to righteous and believing women who are beloved by Allah and His Messenger, mentioned in the Quran in Surah An-Nisa and Surah At-Tahrim, holding a high position in Islam and embodying spiritual significance

data.cultural_impact: The term "Awliyaat" is deeply rooted in Islamic culture and holds a significant place in the Islamic community. The belief in the existence and power of spiritual guides and intercessors has been a central part of Islamic spirituality for centuries. The concept of Awliyaat is often associated with Sufism, an Islamic mystical tradition, and has contributed to the rich and diverse cultural expressions of Islamic spirituality.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spirituality, Awliyaat are considered to be close companions of Allah and are believed to have a special spiritual connection with Him. They are seen as guides and intercessors, and their invocations and blessings are sought after by those who seek peace, guidance, or protection. The belief in the existence and power of spiritual guides and intercessors is a source of comfort and strength for many Muslims, and the reverence for Awliyaat is an essential aspect of Islamic piety and devotion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The term "Awliyaat" in Islamic tradition refers to the saints or friends of Allah. They are those who have a deep spiritual connection with the Divine and serve as intercessors for the believers. Their role is to guide, protect, and inspire, fostering a closer relationship between the believer and Allah.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah, vol. 12, p. 231. The name Awliyaat carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Used to refer to the Sufis who were considered close to Allah and had the ability to intercede on behalf of their followers.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Taymiyyah, Minhaj al-Sunnah al-Nabawiyyah, vol. 4, p. 62. The name Awliyaat carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Referred to as the friends of Allah (Awliya) and the people of Allah (Ashab Allah), who had a special bond with Allah and could seek His forgiveness for the believers.

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Awliyaat' in Islam is used to refer to individuals who have a close relationship with Allah and are considered to be intercessors or protectors for their communities. In the modern context, this concept is seen in various ways across different platforms. On Islamic social media, Awliyaat are often featured as spiritual figures and sources of inspiration, with many accounts and groups dedicated to their teachings and practices. Mobile applications, such as those providing access to Hadiths and Quranic verses, can also serve as a platform for seeking guidance and advice from Awliyaat. Lastly, in community centers and Sufi orders, Awliyaat serve as spiritual leaders and guides, offering personalized advice and support to individuals seeking spiritual growth and enlightenment.
